title: One prompt → a game-ready castle tower built from real Blender operations (134 of them, all editable)
author: Mifsopo_
selftext:
I've been building a free Blender add-on that lets an AI assistant drive Blender's own modeling tools through typed operations, instead of generating a mesh.



The clip is one run from a single sentence: "Model a stone castle tower with battlements, arrow slits and a flag on top, lit for a nice render."



**What happened under the hood:**

`- 42 tool calls, 134 Blender operations (primitives, transforms, booleans for the arrow slits, modifiers, materials, lights, camera)`

`- 4 min 37 s, about $1.55 in model usage`

`- No Python scripts: Python was switched off in that Blender, so every step had to go through a typed operation`

`- The live window in the corner is the actual Blender session, synced to the operation list on the left`



**Why I went this way for game assets:** you get the topology you'd get modeling by hand. Every merlon and slit is a real object you can select, edit, re-UV or delete, and the wireframe at the start of the clip is the actual mesh, not a filter. It's slower than a one-shot generator, but nothing needs retopo before it goes in a game.



It works with any MCP-capable AI assistant. Free download: [https://mifshowcase.store/mifblender](https://mifshowcase.store/mifblender)



Happy to answer questions about how the typed operations work or where it still falls short.

comments.author: WWEtrump
comments.body: typed operations instead of a generated mesh is a neat angle, and the real topology point makes sense. i went the other way with one blender script (about 25k lines) that builds every model in my game. do your arrow slit booleans stay clean when you edit the tower afterwards?

replies.author: Mifsopo_
replies.body:
Good question. In this run they're applied, not live. The add-on applies the boolean on purpose (Exact solver, slits cut one at a time) because a live boolean modifier shows in the viewport but not in the exported FBX, and it checks the mesh for open/non-manifold edges before and after the cut.   
  
So the slits are baked into the tower body: editing the tower afterward is normal mesh editing, but you can't drag a slit and have it re-cut. The cut does leave n-gons around each slit on the cylinder, so it's export-clean rather than quad-perfect.

If I wanted them editable I'd keep the cutters around instead of deleting them, and re-run the cut after changes. Typed ops make that easy to repeat, since every step is a named call you can replay however.

25k lines building every model in your game is serious. Is that one parametric generator, or a script per asset? I'm curious how you handle changes to a model mid-project.

replies.author: WWEtrump
replies.body: one big script, it builds every unit and building in one go. if i want to change a model i edit that part of the script and rerun it, then the new version goes through the same approval before it touches the engine

comments.author: patnard
comments.body:
When I was younger, the fun of 3D modelling came from 3D modelling. I used to feel good helping beginner artist that showed a beginner result like this, asking for feedback and help.

Would you pay personally for a machine that masticate and eat your food only to inject you with the resulting paste to digest yourself?

replies.author: Mifsopo_
replies.body:
this tool is to help streamline the editing process, and automation of blender, with the benefit of streamlining to unreal engine

as far as food, i like my steak medium rare
